title: Provisioning backpressure and safety matrix for Dedicated capacity requests
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and implement a safety-first backpressure and approval matrix for Dedicated capacity provisioning requests. The goal is to prevent overcommit and noisy tenants from saturating fleet capacity, provide predictable throughput guarantees, and automate tiered approvals and provisional capacity with crediting and rollback policies.
background: As Dedicated customers submit capacity requests we have observed bursts that cause headroom exhaustion and SLA violations. Current intake funnels operationally resize or delay requests manually. We need a deterministic system to apply backpressure, provisional allocations, staged approvals, and automatic crediting during probation windows so that the fleet remains healthy without blocking legitimate customer growth.
goals: 1) Reduce urgent manual interventions for capacity spikes by 80% within two quarters. 2) Ensure committed throughput SLOs remain within 5% of targets during steady-state. 3) Standardize a staged approval flow so 95% of routine requests are auto-approved without human review.
success_metrics: % reduction in manual provisioning interventions: target 80%
Mean time to reconcile provisional allocations: <1 business day
acceptance_criteria: A configurable backpressure policy exists that enforces per-customer and per-tenant rate thresholds before hard allocation
Provisional capacity lanes implemented: probation (30d), provisional (7d), committed
Automatic crediting mechanism that grants temporary credits during probation and revokes them on policy breaches
Approval matrix UI in Console with policy overrides and audit log entries for every decision
Integration tests covering overload, rollback, and credit-reconciliation scenarios
Runbook and oncall playbook updated and validated by SRE and Support
proposal: Introduce a three-tier provisioning pipeline: 1) Intake policy evaluates request size, historical usage, and predictive burst score. 2) If safe, grant provisional capacity (probation) with a soft limit and credit token. 3) If request exceeds thresholds, apply backpressure by offering scaled alternatives (lower throughput, scheduled start, or burst-credit purchase) while triggering staged approvals up the matrix. Implement a safety matrix that factors fleet utilization, regional spare capacity, and customer SLA tier to determine auto-approval. Credits are time-bound and reconciled daily; breaches trigger alerts and automatic throttle/rollback.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): implement policy engine and provisional lanes for a small set of low-risk customers (2 weeks). Phase 2 (beta): expand to 25% of new onboarding flows, expose Console settings and escalation UI (4 weeks). Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with monitoring and billing integration, run 30-day monitoring window before full migration (6 weeks).
risks_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative thresholds block legitimate growth. Mitigation: provide override with approval SLA and fast-track path for sales/SEs.
Risk: Incorrect credit reconciliation causing billing discrepancies. Mitigation: nightly reconciliation job and pre-launch shadow accounting matched to billing team.
Risk: Regional imbalances due to provisional allocations. Mitigation: include region-aware capacity factor in safety matrix and limit cross-region provisional moves.
Risk: Complexity for customer support. Mitigation: update playbooks, train Tier 1 support, and add clear UX messaging in Console.
open_questions: What is the probation window for enterprise customers with negotiated SLAs?
How should we price provisional credits if customers consistently use them?
What threshold algorithm (percentile vs absolute units) best predicts harmful bursts?
What manual approval SLA should be promised to sales when customers request overrides?
timeline: Design & policy spec: 2 weeks. Engineering spike and policy engine: 3 weeks. QA & integration tests: 2 weeks. Console UI and runbook updates: 2 weeks. Staged rollout across three phases over 12 weeks.
